tagline: Out over the Sea Islands to a lighthouse made to move.
intro: East of Beaufort, US 21 leaves the town behind and runs out across the Sea Islands, over St. Helena and the tidal marsh of Harbor Island, to the barrier island at the end. The state made it scenic by an act of 1979 that called it simply "a scenic highway". Some call it the Sea Island Scenic Highway.

The road out came in the 1930s, when US 21 was built from St. Helena to Hunting Island, bridges tied the outer islands to Beaufort, and Hunting Island was made a park. Around 1980 the sea took part of the highway, and US 21 now stops where it used to turn toward the lighthouse. The beach has kept washing away since.

moments.title: Saint Helena Island
moments.text: A Sea Island known for its rural Lowcountry character and its Gullah culture and language, where the spiritual "Michael Row the Boat Ashore" originated in the 1860s.

moments.title: Harbor Island
moments.text: Mostly tidal marsh, with US 21 its only road in, and in 2021 the narrow 1939 swing bridge over the Harbor River gave way to a fixed span.

moments.title: Hunting Island State Park
moments.text: The road ends in the park, whose lighthouse was built of bolted cast-iron sections so it could be taken apart, and in 1889, with the tide closing on it, it was moved a mile.
